proof.text: First check the geometry used by the displayed maps. The projections pr_nu:P->P_nu and q_nu:O_nu->U_nu are proper by base change, so p is proper by composition. The map b is a product of the two open immersions, hence open by base change and composition (MorphismProperty.pullbackMap). Its factorization through each open neighborhood inclusion makes v_nu open by cancellation (IsOpenImmersion.of_comp). The projection U->U_1 is separated because it is a base change of e_2 followed by p_2, a composite of separated maps. Since a followed by this projection equals a_1, IsProper.of_comp makes a proper directly. Similarly q_nu z_nu=a_nu and separatedness of q_nu make z_nu proper. The defining pullback projection identities give the remaining equations. These are the complete Lean proofs of b_projections and geometry; the comparison equation is proved in the following two steps.

proof.text: For each projection of the proper ambient product, form the intermediate presentation H=(z_nu,b_nu,p). Its factorization follows from z_nu q_nu=a_nu, the Cartesian side square and p=pr_nu p_nu. Apply proper-ambient graph comparison to identify B_(H,c) with B_(s_nu,c) followed by its compositor--Cartesian-exchange word. Apply open-shrink graph comparison to H and v_nu to identify B_(product,c) with B_(H,c) followed by its inverse triangle and open-compositor word. Reassociate the resulting isomorphisms; their product is definitionally the specified lambda_nu. This proves B_(s_nu,c) followed by lambda_nu equals B_(product,c), for both indices.

Equate the two maps from F_c to the product functor. Compose on the left with the inverse of B_(s,c) and on the right with the inverse of lambda_2. Associativity and inverse cancellation give C_(t,s)=lambda_1 followed by inverse lambda_2, using the definition C_(t,s)=inverse B_(s,c) followed by B_(t,c). This is real Lean isomorphism cancellation; no cocycle, base-change or independence theorem for C is used.
